author: gcormier

title: LDF doesn't evaluate macro properly
rationale: Confirmed LDF bug: chain+/deep+ fails to follow #ifdef-guarded FS.h dependency for Arduino-ESP32 SD_MMC because LDF doesn't evaluate the SOC_SDMMC_HOST_SUPPORTED macro. Workaround (-D flag) confirmed. Recent-ish, labeled known issue.
impl_notes: LDF preprocessor evaluation lives in platformio/builder/tools/piolib.py (LibBuilderBase._process_dependencies / the C-preprocessor conditional evaluation used to resolve #include under #ifdef). The LDF's mini-preprocessor doesn't have SOC_* macros defined by the Arduino-ESP32 SDK, so the `#ifdef SOC_SDMMC_HOST_SUPPORTED` guard hides the FS.h include. Fix: ensure LDF inherits framework/SDK-defined build macros (CPPDEFINES from sdkconfig) when evaluating conditionals, or fall back to scanning all branches when a macro is undefined. Confirmed workaround: -DSOC_SDMMC_HOST_SUPPORTED.

title: Invalid escape character in c_cpp_properties.json

The bug: values containing backslash-escaped characters aren't JSON-escaped when written into the defines array. Ensure defines are serialized via json.dumps (proper escaping) rather than string-interpolated, so backslashes/quotes are valid JSON. Repro with build_flags = -DTEMPLATE_PLACEHOLDER="\'\~\'".

title: pio check using clangtidy fails on large project
rationale: Reproducible bug: `pio check` clangtidy crashes on large projects on Windows due to command-line length limit (Linux works, per comment). Multiple me-toos. The check tool doesn't use the TEMPFILE/response-file path that compile/link use.
impl_notes: platformio/check/tools/clangtidy.py builds a single long clang-tidy invocation with all -I/-D args, which blows past the ~8191-char Windows command limit (piomaxlen.py's TEMPFILE/@response-file handling only wraps CCCOM/CXXCOM/LINKCOM, not the check tools). Fix: for clangtidy/cppcheck on Windows, write the compiler/include args to a response file and pass `@file`, or split invocation. clang-tidy supports passing driver args after `--`; use a temp args file. See ClangTidyCheck.configure_command in clangtidy.py.
author: grisharav

title: Sharing dependencies across environments

impl_notes: Per-env isolation under .pio/libdeps/<env> is intentional (env-specific build flags/platforms). A shared cache could hardlink/symlink or point multiple envs at a shared libdeps dir when the resolved package+version is identical. Look at platformio/package/manager/library.py and the libdeps path construction (project config `libdeps_dir`), plus LDF include-path generation. Must preserve correctness when envs differ in build flags. Effort large; design first.

title: Hook after Clean

Because clean exits early via env.Exit(0), registered Pre/PostActions never fire. Add pre/post hook dispatch around PioClean so extra_scripts and PlatformBase can react (e.g. call registered actions or a platform on_clean(dir) callback before env.Exit). Return the build_dir from PioClean as the reporter suggests.

title: Feature request for support resuming downloads
rationale: Legitimate reliability feature: resumable downloads (HTTP Range) for large package files (e.g. 240MB toolchains), important for flaky connections. Well-scoped in the package downloader.
impl_notes: Package downloading is in platformio/package/download.py (FileDownloader) using requests. Add HTTP Range/resume support: on retry of a partially-downloaded file, send a Range: bytes=<existing>- header, open the target in append mode, and validate with Content-Range / total size; fall back to a full re-download if the server returns 200 instead of 206 or lacks Accept-Ranges. title: Unable to remove library from VS Code
rationale: Windows-specific: package uninstall hits [WinError 5] Access denied on nested paths and leaves files behind. Classic Windows read-only/long-path/locked-file removal issue in the package manager's rmtree.
impl_notes: Package/library removal is in platformio/package/manager/_uninstall.py and the fs helpers in platformio/fs.py (rmtree). On Windows, shutil.rmtree fails with WinError 5 when files are read-only (git-checked-out sources) or paths are locked/long. Add an onerror handler that clears the read-only bit (os.chmod stat.S_IWRITE) and retries, and consider enabling long-path (\\?\) prefixes. This mirrors common shutil.rmtree Windows fixes. impl_notes: Dependency spec parsing/installation is in platformio/package/manager/* (library manager) and the spec parser platformio/package/spec.py. For symlink:/file: schemes the installer should validate the target path exists and raise a clear PackageException when it doesn't (or when the scheme is unknown), instead of logging 'Installing' and returning. Add existence check in the local/symlink install path of the manager's install() flow.

title: Project is built with include directories for two different versions of the same library

title: Support concurrent access to shared PLATFORMIO_PACKAGES_DIR and PLATFORMIO_PLATFORMS_DIR for CI builds

impl_notes: Package/platform install paths are computed in platformio/package/manager/* (base/tool/platform managers) and default to unversioned directory names. Add an opt-in mode using versioned directory names and disabling pruning so concurrent CI builds don't clobber each other. Touches PackageManager path resolution, symlink/unversioned handling, and prune thresholds. Consider file locking around install/extract as a lighter first step.

rationale: Remote agent startup fails on 32-bit Raspbian with an OpenSSL-related error. Likely an environment/OpenSSL-version issue on old 32-bit ARM rather than a core defect. Needs full traceback + confirmation on current release.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the detailed steps. The failure appears to be OpenSSL/environment related on 32-bit Raspbian. Could you paste the complete traceback and the output of `python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)"`, and confirm it still occurs with the latest PlatformIO Core? 32-bit ARM with older OpenSSL is a common source of such errors. We'll follow up or close if it's an environment issue rather than a Core bug.
author: bayrem-gharsellaoui

title: pio debug --interface=gdb --interpreter=mi2 generates malformed GDB-MI messages
rationale: Labeled bug, detailed: GDB-MI output records like @"P"(gdb) lack the required newline before (gdb), violating GDB-MI spec and breaking MI clients. Plausible in PIO's MI stream handling/muxing of gdb-server stdout.
impl_notes: pio debug MI handling is in platformio/debug/ (process/gdb client, output stream muxing). PlatformIO interleaves the gdb-server console output as @-prefixed target-stream records; the newline separating an @"..." record from the following (gdb) prompt is being lost when server stdout arrives in partial chunks. Investigate the MI stream reader/writer that wraps server output and ensure each console/target-stream record is newline-terminated before the prompt. Needs a J-Link/GDB-server setup to reproduce.
author: HanyzPAPU

title: Add support to monorepo style tags for external Git resources
rationale: Concrete package-manager enhancement: support monorepo-style tags/subpaths in lib_deps git URLs (repo.git#subdir@vX). Author offered a PR. Fits the package spec parser in core. Related to #4562/#4366/#3990.
impl_notes: Package spec parsing lives in platformio/package/ (spec.py, PackageSpec, and the VCS/git downloader in package/vcs.py). Extend the git URL fragment grammar to allow a subdirectory path plus tag (e.g. `url.git#libraries/bar@v2.0.1`), resolving the tag as the git ref and the path as the package root within the checkout. Coordinate with author's offered PR.
author: robsonos

title: Add PIO remote agent as a valid `PORT` type for upload, monitor and test.
rationale: Reasonable enhancement to let upload_port/monitor_port/test_port target a remote PIO agent. Touches the proprietary remote component; disposition uncertain, keep open as tracked idea.
author: sticilface

title: Offer to use an available port when the configured port is wrong
rationale: Vague suggestion (empty template body) that when a specified port is invalid PIO could offer an available one. Interactive port fallback risks flashing wrong device. Needs concrete UX before actionable.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the suggestion. Automatically substituting a different serial port when the configured one is missing is risky (it could upload to the wrong device), which is why PlatformIO errors rather than guessing. Could you describe the exact scenario and desired behavior (e.g. a prompt only in interactive TTY sessions, or only when exactly one port is present)? Without a concrete, safe UX we'll keep this parked; note `monitor_port`/`upload_port` already accept globs like `/dev/ttyUSB*` to auto-match.
author: bsheff

title: Support specifying the *exact* library folder for a given environment
rationale: Concrete enhancement to specify exact libdeps folder per-env (to share downloaded deps across envs/projects), with code pointers to install.py. Related to #4451. Valid tracked package-management item, no traction yet.
author: SRGDamia1

title: Debug Mode Adds Unsupported `-g2` Flag to Assembler, Causing Fatal Error
rationale: Real bug: default debug build injects -g2/-ggdb2 into ASFLAGS; arm-none-eabi-as rejects -g2, breaking debug builds with assembly startup files. Workaround (debug_build_flags=-g) confirms cause.
impl_notes: Debug build flags are applied in the build system where debug mode augments CCFLAGS/ASFLAGS (platformio/builder/tools/*, and debug flag handling in platformio/builder/main.py / piobuild.py). The default -g2/-ggdb2 should not be added to assembler flags (ASFLAGS) since 'as' doesn't accept -g2; use -g for the assembler or exclude these from ASFLAGS. Locate where debug '-g2 -ggdb2' is appended and guard against adding to ASFLAGS.
author: AliveGh0st

title: [FEATURE] ability to add custom arguments to cli
rationale: Requests passing custom CLI args to targets/scripts. Already achievable via SCons ARGUMENTS: `pio run -- KEY=VALUE` and reading them in extra_scripts with ARGUMENTS.get(). Answerable; largely a docs gap.
suggested_comment:
This is already possible today. PlatformIO passes trailing SCons variables through, so you can run e.g. `pio run -t mytarget --project-dir . -- SIGN_KEY=/path/key`, and inside an extra script read it with:

```py
from SCons.Script import ARGUMENTS
key = ARGUMENTS.get("SIGN_KEY")
```

See the scripting docs: https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/scripting/. Closing as answered; if you need a more structured argparse-style API beyond SCons ARGUMENTS, please reopen with a concrete use case.
author: fariouche

title: FYI - Build speed optimization - ccache massively speeds up build time
rationale: Very active (65 comments) discussion on native ccache/build-cache support. Workarounds documented (build_cache_dir, IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE) but no first-class ccache integration. High-interest tracked enhancement.
author: zackees

title: Project Inspector fails when projects are compiled with non-native GCC or non-GCC based compilers
rationale: Memory analysis (sizedata) throws AssertionError when the ELF/toolchain isn't native GCC (e.g. TI-ARM). Should fail gracefully or support non-GCC size parsing instead of crashing the build target.
impl_notes: Size/memory analysis is in platformio/builder/tools/piosize.py (invoked as the 'sizedata' action from builder/main.py) and relies on GCC/binutils ELF assumptions. The AssertionError comes from parsing symbol/section data that non-GCC (TI-ARM/clang-based) toolchains produce differently. Wrap the assert paths in defensive checks and degrade gracefully (skip the memory report with a warning) when the ELF/nm/objdump output doesn't match GCC expectations, rather than aborting. Longer-term: allow platform-provided size tooling. Repro uses the unofficial platform-timspm0 with TI-ARM 4.0.0.
author: DSann90

title: Apollo 4 blue lite support
rationale: Really a how-to: can I use a custom-SDK/Makefile MCU in PlatformIO? Answer: yes, via a custom board + dev-platform; board support isn't a core change.
suggested_comment: Yes — PlatformIO can target MCUs with their own vendor SDK, but that support lives in a development platform package plus a custom board JSON, not in platformio-core. You'd create (or reuse) a dev-platform that wraps the Apollo4 SDK/toolchain and add a board definition (https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/platforms/creating_platform.html and creating_board.html). Since there's no core change here, we'll close this; please follow the custom-platform route or ask on the Community Forums for guidance.
author: amir1387aht

title: PIO remote fails on new install (Ubuntu 24.04) due to missing CFFI dependency within penv
rationale: Reproduced by a second user (Python 3.12/3.13 penv). `pio remote agent start` fails with ModuleNotFoundError because cffi (pulled by contrib-pioremote/paramiko) isn't installed in penv. Real packaging bug; manual cffi install fixes it.
impl_notes: cffi is a transitive dependency of the remote agent stack (paramiko/cryptography -> cffi) but isn't guaranteed in the penv on newer Python. Fix in platformio/dependencies.py: ensure cffi (or the remote agent's deps) are declared so get_pip_dependencies/ensure covers it, or have contrib-pioremote package pin its deps. Verify against platformio/remote and the installer penv bootstrap. Confirm whether cryptography/paramiko are declared and add cffi if missing.
author: noisymime

title: Redirecting `pio pkg list` output crashes
rationale: Reproducible UnicodeEncodeError when redirecting `pio pkg list` on Windows: uses print()/raw writes with unicode tree chars (├──) instead of click.echo, which handles Windows unicode. Root cause pinpointed by commenter.
impl_notes: platformio/package/commands/list.py (~lines 102-103) emits unicode box-drawing chars via print/raw stdout, failing under non-UTF8 redirected stdout on Windows. Fix: use click.echo (which handles Windows unicode) throughout the list output, or reconfigure stdout to utf-8, or fall back to ASCII connectors ('+--','|--') when the output encoding can't represent them. Prefer switching to click.echo for the tree lines.
author: AgainPsychoX

title: Platform restrictions on dependencies of submodule in project not honored
rationale: Real LDF/dependency bug: transitive deps of a submodule library ignore the submodule's platforms restriction, installing incompatible libs (ESPAsyncTCP on esp32). Reproducible per reporter; contributor advised filing. Corroborated by CI forum thread.
impl_notes: Bug is in the Library Dependency Finder / lib_compat handling for nested dependencies. See platformio/builder/tools/piolib.py (LibBuilder compatibility filtering) and package dependency resolution. The `platforms`/`frameworks` compat filter is applied to the top-level lib but not propagated when resolving dependencies-of-dependencies pulled from library.json. Need to apply is_platform_compatible/lib_compat_mode recursively during dependency install (package/manager/library.py) and during LDF traversal.
author: Bascy

title: `lib_extra_dirs` deprecated but replacement `lib_deps` only allows packages
rationale: Confusion over deprecation. lib_extra_dirs still works (deprecated but functional); local path deps and symlink:// in lib_deps cover the use case. Multiple users want to add a local folder of libs. Answerable support question.
suggested_comment: Thanks for raising this. `lib_extra_dirs` is deprecated but still functional, and there are supported replacements: you can point `lib_deps` at a local directory using a file/symlink URI, e.g. `lib_deps = symlink://../path/to/your/libs/MyLib` (one entry per library), or place libraries under the project `lib/` folder which is scanned automatically. For a whole tree of ad-hoc sources, `build_src_filter`/adding include paths via `build_flags = -I...` also works. See https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/projectconf/sections/env/options/library/lib_deps.html. If a specific structure still isn't covered, please describe it on the community forum. Closing as answered.
author: raphael-bmec-co

title: Warning when extending from own env
rationale: Confirmed bug: a section extending itself ([base] extends = base) causes ProjectConfig.walk_options to loop forever (no cycle detection). Fix PR #5303 already proposed. Real core hang.
impl_notes: Bug is in ProjectConfig.walk_options in platformio/project/config.py (lines ~170-183): extends_queue/extends_done have no cycle guard, so a self- or mutually-referential 'extends' loops forever. Fix: skip enqueuing a section already in extends_done or extends_queue (and/or raise a clear config error on a detected cycle instead of hanging). A community fix already exists as PR #5303 - review/merge it and add a regression test with [base] extends = base and a longer cycle chain.
author: Unaimend

title: PIO device monitor adds \r before echoed \n automatically
rationale: Serial monitor display behavior; the added CR is almost certainly terminal/TTY (ONLCR) or the pyserial-miniterm console adding CR on newline, not a PIO bug. Best answered/redirected to forum with stty/filter guidance.
suggested_comment: The extra `\r` on display is a terminal/console behavior rather than data being altered on the wire. PlatformIO's monitor is built on pyserial's miniterm; the console renders an incoming `\n` with a carriage return for readability, and your TTY's `ONLCR`/`OPOST` flags can also add one. To confirm nothing is added to the serial data, check with `stty -a < /dev/ttyUSB0`. You likely want a custom monitor filter (see https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/scripting/examples/custom_monitor_filter.html) or a dedicated tool like `tio`. Closing as answered; please continue on the Community Forums.
author: norandomtechie

title: Update SCons dependency to 4.9.0
rationale: Maintainer-filed, concrete dependency bump. Trivial-to-small: update pinned SCons version and run the build test suite. Clear scope, no ambiguity.
impl_notes: Bump the SCons pin in setup.py / pyproject dependencies (and platformio/__init__.py or requirements where SCons version is constrained). Then run the integration/build tests. Watch for SCons 4.9 API deltas affecting platformio/builder/ tools. Verify against the bundled scons in the build environment.
author: ivankravets

title: pio monitor fails when stdin is a pipe
rationale: Clean bug report with full traceback: `echo '' | pio run -t monitor` crashes with 'Inappropriate ioctl for device' because the monitor assumes a TTY on stdin. Should degrade gracefully when stdin isn't a terminal (common in CI).
impl_notes: In platformio/device/monitor/ (command.py / terminal handling) the miniterm console tries termios/tcgetattr on stdin which fails when stdin is a pipe (not a TTY). Guard the interactive console setup with sys.stdin.isatty(); when not a TTY, skip raw-mode setup / disable the input thread (monitor becomes read-only) instead of raising. Reproduce with `echo '' | pio run -t monitor`.
author: Raupinger

title: Pre/Post Actions on buildprog not called
rationale: User attaches Pre/Post actions to 'buildprog' target, which isn't the node they think. Actions must target the actual build node ($BUILD_DIR/${PROGNAME}.elf) or $PROGPATH; 'buildprog' is an alias, not a file node. Support answer, not a bug.
suggested_comment: `AddPreAction`/`AddPostAction` attach to build *nodes* (files/targets in the SCons graph), and `buildprog` isn't a node you can hook that way. To run code before/after the firmware is built, attach to the program node, e.g. `env.AddPreAction("$BUILD_DIR/${PROGNAME}.elf", test)` and `env.AddPostAction("$BUILD_DIR/${PROGNAME}.elf", test2)` (or `"buildprog"` for upload-related targets like `upload`). See https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/scripting/actions.html for the list of hookable targets. Closing as answered — reopen if that doesn't work for you.
author: seby42

title: pio debug --interface=gdb --interpreter=mi2 does not wrap diagnostics messages into proper format
rationale: Reproducible bug filed by a contributor (elmot): in gdb MI2 mode, diagnostic/error output from the debug server isn't wrapped into well-formed MI records (missing ^error,msg=...). Related to #4959/#4565. Affects MI clients.
impl_notes: The debug server/gdb bridge in platformio/debug/ (process/server.py and the MI output handling in debug/process/*) forwards inferior/server stderr lines raw instead of wrapping them as MI async/stream/result records when --interpreter=mi2 is active. Fix: when MI mode is detected, escape and wrap out-of-band diagnostic text as `~"..."`/`^error,msg=...` records. See related #4959 and #4565. Requires detecting interpreter=mi2 from the debug invocation and filtering server output accordingly.
author: elmot

title: Building a library without linking attempt
rationale: Well-argued gap: no way to build a pure library project (compile + archive, no link) so CI fails on missing main()/setup()/loop(). libarchive/lib_archive don't address it. Maintainer engaged.
impl_notes: Build orchestration is in platformio/builder/main.py and builder/tools/ (piobuild.py, piotarget.py). Add a project/env option (e.g. build type = library|application, default application) that, for library projects, stops after compiling + creating the static archive (.a) and skips the ELF link target, plus a general compile-only build option (build without linking). Would need to register a distinct default target that doesn't require main()/setup()/loop(). Coordinate with the existing 'buildprog'/link targets so `pio run` picks the right terminal target.
author: matthiashanns

title: python curses module fails to load on MacOS Ventura
rationale: The bundled portable Python's _curses.so was built for macOS 14.3 and won't load on older macOS (Ventura) against system libncurses. This is a portable-python package build issue, not core code; fix is in the python package build. Redirect.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the report. The `_curses` module here comes from the portable Python package PlatformIO downloads, and this specific `.so` was built against a newer macOS SDK than Ventura, causing the `_is_pad` symbol mismatch against the system libncurses. That's a build issue in the portable-python package rather than platformio-core code. We'll track it on the packaging side; as a workaround, upgrading the OS or using a system Python for Core avoids the bundled binary. Closing the core issue.
author: PhracturedBlue

title: extra_script global defines not working
rationale: User can't get global CPPDEFINES from a library extraScript to reach the build command; maintainer suggested PRE action but user says docs example uses no pre and fails. Possible doc/behavior mismatch; needs a clean minimal repro to determine bug vs misuse.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the detailed report. There are two separate things here: a library `build.extraScript` runs in the library's build env, while a project `extra_scripts` should use a `pre:` script and modify `DefaultEnvironment()` before the build graph is created for global defines to take effect. To help us pin down whether this is a docs mismatch or a bug, could you attach a minimal complete project (platformio.ini + the exact script + a one-file src) that reproduces it on the latest Core? With that we can confirm the expected behavior and fix the documentation or the code accordingly.
author: Levi--G

title: Sibling folders
rationale: User wants source lib and unit tests in sibling (not child) folders and resorts to symlinks. Addressable via lib_deps symlink://, custom test build config, and project structure guidance. Support question, no core change obviously needed.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the question. PlatformIO expects tests under the `test/` directory, but you can keep your library sources elsewhere and wire them in without symlinks: point `lib_deps = symlink://../../src/estd` (relative to the project) so the library is resolved from a sibling folder, and use per-environment `test_filter`/`build_src_filter` to scope which sources compile. That usually removes the need for the symlink hacks that confuse VS Code. If you can share a minimal layout on the community forum (https://community.platformio.org) we can suggest the exact config. Closing as answered.
author: malachib

title: COMPILATIONDB_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN=True skips WiFi
rationale: Not a core bug: with COMPILATIONDB_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN clangd resolves toolchain headers but library headers scope out. Comment provides working solution (drop the option, use clangd --query-driver). Answer and close.
suggested_comment: This is a clangd configuration trade-off rather than a PlatformIO defect. Instead of `COMPILATIONDB_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN=True`, keep the default compilation database and let clangd discover the toolchain headers by adding `--query-driver=/**/.platformio/**/bin/*-g++,/**/.platformio/**/bin/*-gcc` to your clangd arguments. That resolves both library headers (WiFi.h) and standard headers (`<algorithm>`) simultaneously. Closing as answered; please re-open if that doesn't work for you.
author: sakhnik

title: Library with `libCompatMode: strict` is not actually being strict
rationale: Reproducible LDF bug (confirmed by a second reporter): a library's `build.libCompatMode: strict` isn't propagated to its transitive dependencies (e.g. RPAsyncTCP via ESPAsyncWebServer), so incompatible-platform deps still get built. Labeled help wanted.
impl_notes: In platformio/builder/tools/piolib.py, libCompatMode is read per-library from its manifest; it isn't inherited by dependency LibBuilders during dependency resolution. When a parent library sets libCompatMode=strict, propagate that compat mode to the LibBuilders it pulls in (or enforce that a dep declaring incompatible `platforms` is skipped under strict). Also relates to #3915 (extra_script/compat). The deeper fix is honoring each dep's own `platforms` field: RPAsyncTCP declares platforms=raspberrypi and should be excluded on espressif32. Effort medium; add LDF tests with a strict parent + platform-limited transitive dep.
author: Lenart12

title: Spaces in Windows User name not supported in Inspect
rationale: Confirmed real bug: in check/tools/base.py the toolchain-defines command interpolates an unquoted includes_file path into a shell=True command, so paths with spaces (e.g. C:\Users\Wim Foo) break with 'not recognized as a command'.
impl_notes: platformio/check/tools/base.py, `_get_toolchain_defines._extract_defines` (~line 89-101). The cmd string `'echo | "%s" -x %s %s %s -dM -E -'` interpolates `includes_file` (the last %s) without quotes, and it's run with shell=True. When the includes file path (derived from a dir with spaces, e.g. C:\Users\Wim ...) is unquoted, the shell splits on the space. Fix: quote the includes_file argument (and audit the @file / -I paths it references) or better, avoid shell=True by passing an argv list and feeding the `echo` input via stdin. Reporter's `check_skip_packages = yes` merely sidesteps it. Add a test with a path containing spaces.
author: wvdvegt

title: Neovim + Arduino + PlatformIO
rationale: Support question about arduino-language-server/clangd LSP for .ino files under Neovim. Not a Core bug; community workaround (.clangd generator, compiledb) exists. Belongs on forums.
suggested_comment: PlatformIO generates a clangd-compatible `compile_commands.json` via `pio run -t compiledb`, which is the recommended path for LSP with Neovim (point clangd at it). The arduino-language-server expects the Arduino CLI and isn't part of the PIO toolchain, hence the config error. A community helper for generating `.clangd` for PlatformIO projects is here: https://github.com/gunlock/pio-clangd. Since this is an editor-integration/support question rather than a Core bug, we're closing it; the Community Forums are the best place to continue.
author: csdarren

title: ExtraScripts: Allow hooking on errors
rationale: Reasonable scripting enhancement: run extra-script hooks on build/upload failure (e.g. AddErrorAction / a post-'error' action). Fits AddPreAction/AddPostAction machinery. No objections, well-scoped.
impl_notes: Extra-script actions are wired via env.AddPreAction/AddPostAction in platformio/builder/. SCons doesn't natively run post-actions on failed builds. Options: register an atexit/SCons Taskmaster failure hook, or wrap targets to invoke a user-supplied 'error' action on non-zero exit. Expose an env.AddErrorAction(target, callback) API in the builder tools and document it. Investigate builder/tools/piomisc.py and main.py.
author: Lenart12

title: symlinks in platformio.ini should use pre-binding to path instead of late binding
rationale: Reports symlink:// with '..' relative paths resolving against ~/.platformio instead of the project dir. Plausible bug but terse; needs a minimal repro (exact platformio.ini + cwd + observed vs expected path) to confirm the resolution base.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the report. To investigate the `symlink://` path resolution, could you share a minimal repro: the exact `lib_deps`/`platform_packages` line, the directory you run `pio` from, and the resolved path you see vs. what you expect? In particular, whether the base should be the project dir or the config file's dir. `symlink://` paths are resolved relative to the project directory; a concrete example with `..` will let us confirm whether the base is wrong. We'll pick this up once we can reproduce.
author: zackees

title: Upgrade cppcheck again!
rationale: Bundled tool-cppcheck is stale (dependencies.py pins ~1.21100.0 ~ cppcheck 2.11) vs upstream 2.17+. Recurring request (see #4571). Bump the packaged version.
impl_notes: platformio/dependencies.py line ~23 pins 'tool-cppcheck': '~1.21100.0'. Requires publishing a newer tool-cppcheck package (2.17.x) to the registry, then bumping this constraint. Core change is one line; the real work is repackaging the tool. Also worth considering letting users pin the cppcheck version (see #5285 discussion). Coordinate with the tool package maintainers.
author: red-scorp

title: New Board BMduino(BM53A367A) Holtek
rationale: Board/MCU support (Holtek HT32/BMduino) belongs in a dev-platform repo (Holtek even ships an Arduino package index), not core.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the detailed request. Board and MCU support (Holtek HT32 / BMduino) is added via a PlatformIO development platform package, not platformio-core (https://github.com/topics/platformio-platform). Since Holtek already publishes an Arduino package index, a community dev-platform could wrap it. There's no core change here, so we'll close this; please track it against the relevant platform.
author: XiaXia009

title: [feature] DFP (Device Family Pack) / atpack / CMSIS integration with PlatformIO
rationale: Broad, exploratory idea to integrate CMSIS-Pack/atpack device metadata (registers, SVD, memory maps) into PIO. Author built parsers/viewers. Large and cross-cutting (registry/platform/VSCode) but a legitimately interesting roadmap discussion; not obviously implementable now.
author: s-celles

title: `pio device monitor` doesn't reconnect proactively when resetting ESP32
rationale: Legit gap: monitor only detects disconnect after a failed write (user keypress), so it can't auto-reconnect proactively to capture setup() logs. Reporter offered a PR with a keepalive approach. Reasonable device-monitor enhancement.
impl_notes: Device monitor is in platformio/device/monitor/ (terminal + filters). Auto-reconnect currently triggers on a write/read exception. Add an optional proactive liveness check (periodic port poll / keepalive) so disconnects are detected without user input, then reconnect. Reporter proposed a background keepalive thread; guard it behind an option to avoid interfering with devices sensitive to stray bytes.
author: riywo

title: Add dynamic interpolation for package paths
rationale: Well-argued core feature by a contributor (maxgerhardt), 13-comment design discussion. Add ${packages.<name>} interpolation resolving to the actual installed package dir (versioned/symlinked), replacing fragile ${platformio.packages_dir}/tool-x paths. Clear need, clear API.
impl_notes: Add a new interpolation namespace in the project config parser (platformio/project/config.py) e.g. ${packages.tool-avrdude} that resolves via PlatformBase.get_package_dir(). Config interpolation currently supports ${platformio.*}, ${sysenv.*}, ${this.*}; extend the resolver to look up the active platform's installed package path lazily. Handles versioned dirs (tool-avrdude@1.70100.0) and symlink:// packages. Needs platform context available at config-render time.
author: maxgerhardt

title: How to manually specify the download server
rationale: Support question: user wants to pin the package download mirror/source. Related PR discussion shows the server-side mirror scheduling can't currently be overridden by users; answer with current behavior and env vars.
suggested_comment: PlatformIO resolves package downloads through a registry HEAD request that redirects to a mirror (see `RegistryFileMirrorIterator` in `platformio/registry/mirror.py`); the specific mirror is chosen server-side and there is currently no public option to force a particular download host from the client. You can point the whole registry/mirror set via the `__registry_mirror_hosts__` / `PLATFORMIO_...` configuration, but per-download source pinning isn't exposed. If you need this for a restricted/accelerated network, please describe your setup and we can treat it as a feature request; otherwise I'll close this as a support question.
author: Kreedb

title: Undefines in build_flags don't work if there's a space after -U
rationale: Reproducible bug: `-U MACRO` (with space) is mishandled - SCons splits into ['-U','MACRO'] and only '-U' is captured (undef[2:] empty), breaking builds. Root cause identified; a contributor volunteered a PR.
impl_notes: platformio/builder/tools/piobuild.py, ProcessFlags(): the undefines extraction assumes '-UMACRO' single-token form and does undef[2:]. When space-separated, CCFLAGS contains ['-U','MACRO']. Iterate CCFLAGS with an index: when a token equals '-U', consume the next token as the macro name (mirroring how '-D'/defines are paired), otherwise strip the '-U' prefix. Add tests for both '-UM' and '-U M' forms. A contributor (SpacePlushy) offered a PR.
author: aveao

title: Add flag to disable self-upgrades
rationale: Concrete, low-risk packaging feature requested by Fedora/Debian/Arch/OpenWrt maintainers who all currently patch out `pio upgrade`. A build-time/env flag to disable the upgrade command removes recurring downstream patching.
impl_notes: The upgrade command is platformio/commands/upgrade.py, and update checks live in platformio (self-update logic, e.g. platformio/__init__.py version checks and maintenance/telemetry). Add a build/runtime switch - simplest is an env var (e.g. PLATFORMIO_DISABLE_UPGRADE / a setting) that makes `pio upgrade` exit with a clear 'managed by your system package manager' message and disables background update nags. Distros can set it instead of patching. Document it. Matches the Fedora short-circuit-upgrades patch behavior.
author: vidplace7

title: Bug: build_src_flags has an impact on lib_deps
rationale: Terse report (mainly cross-links to #4667, #4253, #4578); claims build_src_flags like -Wpedantic leak into library/dependency compilation. Plausible but needs a minimal reproducible example to confirm and localize.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the report. To act on this we need a minimal, self-contained reproducer: a small `platformio.ini` plus source tree showing `build_src_flags` (e.g. `-Wpedantic`) affecting the compilation of a `lib_deps` library, with the verbose build output (`pio run -v`) demonstrating the flag applied to the library's translation units. `build_src_flags` is meant to apply only to `src/`, so a concrete case will help us pinpoint the leak. Could you attach that?
author: omani

title: Bug: sin1.contabostorage.com blocked by QUAD9 (DoH) DNS-over-HTTPS leads to DNS flood
rationale: Real, recurring bug (multiple reporters, 4 reactions, labeled help wanted): when a mirror is unreachable (SSL/connection refused/DNS-blocked), core retries the SAME failing mirror endlessly at high rate instead of advancing/backing off. Related to #5062.
impl_notes: Two layers. (1) platformio/package/manager/_registry.py install loop iterates `RegistryFileMirrorIterator`; on network/SSL failure it just logs 'Looking for another mirror...' and re-enters __next__. (2) platformio/registry/mirror.py advances only when the server returns a NEW X-PIO-Mirror header; if the HEAD/redirect keeps pointing at the same dead mirror (or the failure is at connect time), _visited_mirrors never grows and it loops without bound. Fix: cap total attempts / add exponential backoff, treat a connection/SSL failure to a given host as 'visited' so it's bypassed, and stop after all distinct mirrors are exhausted with a clear error. Also consider dropping/repairing the failing contabostorage mirror server-side. Effort medium; add a test simulating a persistently failing mirror.

title: Unexpected error occours when specifying a custom directory to device monitor
rationale: Reproducible FileNotFoundError when running `pio device monitor -d <subdir>` (project dir override). A second user confirms. Traceback points to CLI/config loading not handling the -d/project-dir path for monitor. Real bug.
impl_notes: `pio device monitor -d` sets the project directory; the monitor command (platformio/device/monitor/command.py) then loads platformio.ini / resolves paths and hits FileNotFoundError. Likely the project-dir option isn't propagated consistently to config lookup or a path is resolved relative to cwd instead of the given -d. Reproduce with `pio device monitor -d examples/<x>/` and trace where the missing file path is computed; fix path resolution to honor the -d project dir.
author: renanrms

title: VSCode IntelliSense `forcedInclude` doesn't work
rationale: Confirmed in code: c_cpp_properties.json.tpl emits forcedInclude entries via _find_forced_includes/_find_abs_path, but relative project paths (e.g. include/forcedInclude.hpp) that aren't in the include-path list stay relative, which cpptools can't resolve. All other include paths are already absolute. Clear, small fix.
impl_notes: File: platformio/project/integration/tpls/vscode/.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json.tpl. `_find_forced_includes` calls `_find_abs_path(inc, inc_paths)`, which only resolves against known include dirs; a project-relative path like `include/forcedInclude.hpp` falls through and is emitted relative. Fix: when the resolved path is still relative, join it against the project root (workspace folder) to emit an absolute path, matching how other includePaths are absolutized. Verify with build_flags `-include "include/forcedInclude.hpp"`.

title: PIO platform Longan Nano GD32 bricked
rationale: Not 'bricked hardware' — install fails because the sipeed platform-gd32v pulls toolchain-gd32v from the registry and gets 'You do not have permission' (registry entry sipeed/gd32v unavailable). This is a third-party platform/registry package issue, not a core defect. Reporter already links the sipeed platform repo issue.
suggested_comment: Thanks for the report — and note your board isn't bricked; this is a package-resolution failure. The `sipeed/platform-gd32v` platform references `platformio/toolchain-gd32v` from the registry, and that package/owner is returning 'You do not have permission', which is a problem with that third-party platform and its registry packages rather than platformio-core. The right place to track this is the platform repo (you've already linked sipeed/platform-gd32v#40). As a workaround, community forks of platform-gd32v that vendor a working RISC-V toolchain generally install correctly. Closing here as it's not a core issue; please follow up on the platform repo.

title: Home: Could not load recent projects
rationale: PIO Home 'could not load recent projects' with an offline/no-internet message. This is a PIO Home (home) / VSCode-extension surface, not core CLI; the message indicates the user is offline. Redirect + explain.
suggested_comment: The message you're seeing ("You are not connected to the Internet...") means PlatformIO Home couldn't reach the network - on a first build it needs connectivity to install platforms/toolchains. Please check your internet/proxy/firewall and retry; once dependencies are cached, subsequent builds work offline. PlatformIO Home and the IDE UI are maintained in the platformio-home / platformio-vscode-ide repositories rather than platformio-core, so if this persists with a working connection please report it there with details. Closing here as this isn't a Core issue.

title: Libraries not installed from registry cannot be detected as already installed dependencies of other libraries
rationale: Recent, detailed, plausible: libs installed from GitHub/non-registry have empty owner field, so a dependency spec with owner can't match the already-installed lib, causing redundant re-install. Real dependency-matching bug in package manager.
impl_notes: Dependency matching is in platformio/package/manager/ (base/library manager) + package/meta.py PackageSpec. Non-registry installs don't record an 'owner' (not read from library.json/library.properties), but dependency specs include owner, so the installed-package match fails and the dep is re-installed. Fix: when matching an installed package against a dependency spec, match by name (and repo URL) when owner is unknown, or persist/derive owner for non-registry installs. Look at how get_package/find matches PackageSpec fields.
